notes: Falco reported Sensitive file opened for reading by non-trusted program for /etc/shadow.
Tracee observed the openat syscall for /etc/shadow from the cat process inside the Alpine container. This establishes file-access telemetry visibility under the configured execve+openat event set.

Tetragon captured the sched_process_exec telemetry for /bin/cat and, under the ebpf-lab-file-access tracing policy, recorded a sys_openat event whose pathname argument is /etc/shadow. Pathname-specific visibility of the sensitive-file open is therefore established at the telemetry level. This is kernel/event visibility only: no alerting policy evaluated the open as a security detection, so this is telemetry observed, not a confirmed detection.

Tetragon observed sched_process_exec telemetry for sh, id, uname inside the controlled Alpine container. Container metadata (cgroup id) was enriched on each exec event. This is telemetry observed, not a confirmed security detection (no alerting policy was evaluated).
The network test generated process-execution detections. This result does not establish that Falco's network-specific rules detected the connection.

No network/connect tracing policy is configured in this lab, so no socket-level connection event was captured and network-specific detection is not established. openat telemetry for TLS material (libssl/cert store) was incidentally observed.

5 deterministic trials of the benign baseline workload. All 5 trials produced the identical process-execution chain ['sh', 'id'] with [2] exec event(s). This is exploratory repeatability evidence (small n), described rather than aggregated into a statistical claim. Telemetry observed, not a security detection.

Both the sensitive read (/etc/shadow) and the benign read (/etc/alpine-release) produced openat telemetry with the correct pathname argument under the ebpf-lab-file-access policy. Tetragon's tracing policy captures the pathname for both but raises no alert for either — it does not distinguish sensitive from benign at the detection layer (no alerting rule configured). The distinction exists in the telemetry (pathname), not in a detection verdict.
